`TestHeterogeneousRegisteredIdentities` parametrizes `build_model_evaluation_surface` over both `IDENTITY_FIXED_WIDTH` and `IDENTITY_ADAPTIVE_RANGE`; both build deterministic schema-bound surfaces, each recording its own registry / schema identity, version and checksum. `test_fixed_width_rejects_adaptive_only_axis` confirms that an axis declared only by the T065 adaptive schema (`five_minute_window_seconds`) is refused by the T062 fixed-width schema via T106's `UndeclaredAxisError`; `test_adaptive_accepts_axis_shared_with_baselines` confirms a shared axis (`tick_spacing`) is accepted on both. `WalkForwardFold` records `train_start_decision_time`, `train_end_decision_time`, `eval_start_decision_time`, `eval_end_decision_time`, `purge_plus_embargo_seconds` (all non-negative ints). The `__post_init__` rejects `train_end <= train_start`, `eval_end <= eval_start`, and a `gap < purge_plus_embargo_seconds`. Point-in-time, machine-recorded folds are reproducible from the input — `to_dict()` exposes every boundary; `WalkForwardEvaluationInputs` carries the fold tuple alongside the binding identity and surface checksum.

`compute_episode_bootstrap_intervals` returns four rows (`rule.net_return_q64_64`, `model.net_return_q64_64`, `delta.net_return_q64_64`, `ratio.net_return_q64_64`) using a deterministic LCG seeded by `parameters.bootstrap_seed` and `parameters.bootstrap_iterations`; the percentile bounds helper uses the symmetric Q64.64 alpha. `test_intervals_are_deterministic` confirms repeated calls return identical `lower_q64_64` / `upper_q64_64`. `compute_regime_conditional_breakdown` always emits one row per `REGIME_LABELS_FOR_BREAKDOWN` label (`RANGE`, `UP_TREND`, `DOWN_TREND`, `JUMP_RISK`) with zero counts when episodes are absent, so a favourable aggregate cannot hide a loss concentrated in one market state and a losing pool/regime/fold is not dropped.

`build_rejection_record` returns a `RejectionRecord` whose `reason_code` is `PREDICTION_UP_ECONOMICS_DOWN` when the prediction metric improves (LOWER_IS_BETTER) but the LP-economics mean (`net_return_q64_64`) does not; when both improve it returns `None`. A zero-episode fold yields `None` (no rejection), but `parameters_min_episodes_default()` is 5 and `ECONOMICS_DOWN_EPISODE_UNDERFLOW` fires when the floor is below the observation count. The verdict comes from simulated LP economics (`net_return_q64_64` mean), not from a prediction metric.

`evaluate_out_of_distribution` returns `VERDICT_UNCERTAIN` (with no position emitted) when (a) `handle is None`, (b) `schema_revision` / `code_revision` / `registry_checksum` are empty or `UNKNOWN`, (c) `trained_at_unix_seconds + staleness_seconds < evaluation_decision_time` (when `staleness_seconds > 0`), (d) `evaluation_pool_key_id` is disjoint from `training_pool_set` (when `require_pool_set_membership=True`), and (e) `predictions` is constant (`unique_values <= ood_prediction_variance_q64_64`). When `predictions is None` the gate skips (e). The model-backed regime and fee-opportunity components translate the verdict into a `RegimeAssessment.uncertain(...)` / `FeeOpportunityAssessment.uncertain(...)` whose `model_version` is `MODEL_COMPONENT_VERSION`; no position / size / tick range is emitted by the model layer.

`ModelBackedRegimeModel.assess` and `ModelBackedFeeOpportunityModel.assess` consume the same T060 `MarketSnapshot`/`PortfolioSnapshot` inputs as the rule implementations, never mutate them, and return a `RegimeAssessment` / `FeeOpportunityAssessment` carrying the contract's `version` and the `MODEL_COMPONENT_VERSION`. When the OOD gate yields `UNCERTAIN` the components emit `RegimeAssessment.uncertain(...)` / `FeeOpportunityAssessment.uncertain(...)` with the gate's reason in `notes`; when the rule fallback is supplied AND the handle is `None` the rule's assessment is returned unchanged; the rule fallback is never consulted as a second authority over the model's own verdict. All 80 T060 tests still pass, so the same dependency and interface tests that protect the rule implementation continue to pass.

`check_robustness_evidence` accepts `None` (returns `MISSING`), a `ParameterSurface` carrying `LEGACY_SURFACE_MARKER` (returns `LEGACY_ONLY`), or a `SchemaBoundParameterSurface` (compares its binding identity against the run's `ValidatedManifestBinding`). A mismatch returns `REVISION_MISMATCH`. An unregistered-identity binding against a schema-bound surface returns `REVISION_MISMATCH` because `is_schema_bound_surface_identity` checks `is_registered(strategy_identity)`. The unbound T064 builder (`build_parameter_surface`) is rejected by the gate (`test_t064_surface_yields_legacy_only_status`). The walk-forward orchestrator only emits a rejection record when `RobustnessEvidenceStatus.CURRENT`, otherwise the rejection record is `None` — so missing, legacy-only or revision-mismatched evidence blocks publication of the robustness conclusion rather than substituting the unrestricted T064 surface.

`build_model_evaluation_surface` returns a `ModelEvaluationSurface` whose `surface_checksum` is the T106 surface's `checksum()`; the surface's `binding_identity` is the T106 `surface_identity`. Repeated construction over the same `surface_id`, `binding`, and `axes` returns the same `surface_checksum` (`test_surface_checksum_is_deterministic`). `test_surface_builds_for_fixed_width` and `test_surface_builds_for_adaptive` show each surface records its own `binding.strategy_identity` and registry checksum; a registry / schema revision produces a different binding identity and a different checksum.

`LegacyRobustnessFixture` accepts only legacy `ParameterSurface` instances carrying the explicit `LEGACY_SURFACE_MARKER` (enforced by `is_legacy_surface` and the marker check); the fixture's `to_legacy_dict()` returns `self.legacy_surface.to_dict()` (byte-identical across calls); a fixture with the wrong marker raises `EvaluationError`. The T102 robustness gate accepts legacy surfaces only as `LEGACY_ONLY` evidence (the artifact cannot be consumed as current robustness evidence); T106 schema-bound surfaces are not merged with the legacy artifact.

Current evaluation never calls `build_parameter_surface` (the T064 builder). The only path that accepts a surface is `check_robustness_evidence`, and a T064 `ParameterSurface` (legacy marker on by construction) returns `LEGACY_ONLY`. The schema-bound surface builder (`build_model_evaluation_surface`) requires a registered identity and `is_registered` enforces the closed vocabulary. So current evaluation cannot construct a parameter surface through the unrestricted T064 builder; a legacy artifact offered as current evaluation evidence is refused.

`walk_forward_evaluate_model` validates inputs, calls `check_robustness_evidence` first (so missing/legacy/mismatched evidence is recorded before any fold runs), then iterates folds calling `rule_runner` and `model_runner` (both `EpisodeRunner` callables; the orchestrator rejects non-tuple returns), aggregates episodes, computes bootstrap intervals and the regime breakdown, emits the rejection record only when `RobustnessEvidenceStatus.CURRENT`, and returns a `ModelEvaluationReport` carrying the binding identity, surface checksum, fold list, episode counts, intervals, breakdowns, rejection, and robustness check. `test_evaluation_with_current_robustness`, `test_evaluation_with_missing_robustness_blocks_publication`, `test_evaluation_with_revision_mismatch_blocks_publication`, and `test_evaluation_rejects_non_tuple_runner_return` exercise the happy path, the two block-publication paths, and the runner-validation path respectively.
